docs.title: About nist-ai-rmf
docs.text:
nist-ai-rmf is an umbrella LinkML schema for the NIST AI Risk Management Framework family. It does not redefine any classes, slots, enums, or types of its own - it simply pulls together two sibling schemas that are maintained in their own repositories:

Import Source repository Models nist_ai_100_1 lmodel/nist-ai-100-1 AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1): foundational concepts, Core Functions / Categories / Subcategories, Profiles, design attributes, AI RMF Playbook companion data nist_ai_600_1 lmodel/nist-ai-600-1 GAI Profile (NIST AI 600-1): 12 GAI risks, Suggested Actions, Primary GAI Considerations, Structured Public Feedback methods

The sub-schemas are resolved over the network via the schema_100_1: and schema_600_1: prefixes declared in src/nist_ai_rmf/schema/nist_ai_rmf.yaml; they are not vendored into this repository.

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
nist_ai_rmf  (umbrella, this repo)
                     /          \
            nist_ai_100_1 ----- nist_ai_600_1
                    \            /
                  nist_ai_rmf_common  (hosted in nist-ai-100-1)
  • Both sub-schemas import a shared nist_ai_rmf_common module (hosted in nist-ai-100-1) that defines the one canonical base — the NamedThing root, identifier/title/description slots, SubcategoryCode, and TrustworthinessCharacteristicEnum. This is what lets the two be merged into one namespace without colliding.
  • Elements re-export under the nist_ai_rmf: default prefix, so downstream consumers import only this umbrella to access everything.
  • Where the two NIST documents genuinely diverge — the AI lifecycle stages and actor-task vocabularies differ between 100-1 and 600-1 — the GAI Profile keeps its own GaiLifecycleStageEnum / GaiActorTaskEnum as class-local attributes on GaiRisk / SuggestedAction, so both taxonomies survive the merge intact.
  • Two tree-root classes are exposed by the imports:
  • AiRmfFramework - from nist_ai_100_1
  • GaiProfile - from nist_ai_600_1 Callers must pass --target-class when running linkml-validate.
  • SSSOM cross-vocabulary mappings, per-element example fixtures, and the NIST AI RMF Playbook validator all live in the upstream repositories and are exercised by their own CI.

docs.title: What this repository ships
docs.text:
• The single umbrella schema (src/nist_ai_rmf/schema/nist_ai_rmf.yaml).
  • Merged-schema generation targets under project/ (JSON Schema, OWL, SHACL, ShEx, GraphQL, Pydantic, etc.) produced from the umbrella with all imports inlined.
  • Merged-only unit tests under tests/ that verify both imports resolve and that classes/enums from each sub-schema are reachable through the merged nist_ai_rmf namespace.

docs.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
docs.text:
Merged LinkML schema for the NIST AI Risk Management Framework family.

Imports: * nist_ai_100_1 - AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1) foundational concepts, Core Functions / Categories / Subcategories, Profiles, design attributes, and the AI RMF Playbook companion data shape. * nist_ai_600_1 - GAI Profile (NIST AI 600-1): 12 GAI risks, Suggested Actions, Primary GAI Considerations, and Structured Public Feedback methods.

Most consumers should import this umbrella to get the entire framework via a single namespace (nist_ai_rmf:). Two tree-root classes are exposed by the imports - AiRmfFramework from the core module and GaiProfile from the GAI module - so callers must pass --target-class when validating.

Merged LinkML schema for the NIST AI Risk Management Framework family.

Imports: * nist_ai_100_1 - AI RMF 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1) foundational concepts, Core Functions / Categories / Subcategories, Profiles, design attributes, and the AI RMF Playbook companion data shape. * nist_ai_600_1 - GAI Profile (NIST AI 600-1): 12 GAI risks, Suggested Actions, Primary GAI Considerations, and Structured Public Feedback methods.

Most consumers should import this umbrella to get the entire framework via a single namespace (nist_ai_rmf:). Two tree-root classes are exposed by the imports - AiRmfFramework from the core module and GaiProfile from the GAI module - so callers must pass --target-class when validating.

The outcome statement of a Category or Subcategory - the desired

result of carrying out its actions.

docs.title: Slot: primary_considerations
docs.text:
The primary GAI considerations from Appendix A (Governance,

Pre-Deployment Testing, Content Provenance, Incident

Disclosure). Discriminated by consideration_kind.

docs.title: Slot: profile_type
docs.text: The kind of AI RMF Profile.

docs.title: Slot: profiles
docs.text: AI RMF profiles defined alongside this Framework instance.

docs.title: Slot: provenance_techniques
docs.text:
For Content Provenance: provenance data tracking techniques

such as digital watermarking, metadata recording, digital

fingerprinting, and human authentication (Appendix A.1.6).

docs.title: Slot: published_date
docs.text: Date the document was published.

docs.title: Slot: publisher
docs.text: The publisher of the document (e.g., NIST).

docs.title: Slot: red_team_type
docs.text: The type of AI red-teaming exercise.

docs.title: Slot: references_text
docs.text:
Free-text list of references, citations, and supporting

resources. Corresponds to the AI RMF Playbook "References"

section.

docs.title: Slot: related_impacts
docs.text: The impacts that contribute to a risk.

docs.title: Slot: risk_categorization
docs.text:
Higher-level categorisation - technical/model, misuse, or

ecosystem/societal.

docs.title: Slot: risk_measurement_challenges
docs.text: Identified challenges in measuring AI risk.

docs.title: Slot: risk_response
docs.text: The chosen risk treatment option.

docs.title: Slot: risk_scope
docs.text: Scope levels at which the risk may manifest.

docs.title: Slot: risk_sources
docs.text: Sources from which the risk may emerge.

docs.title: Slot: section_about
docs.text: Free-text discussion ("About" section).

docs.title: Slot: section_actions
docs.text: Bulleted suggested actions ("Actions" section).

docs.title: Slot: section_doc
docs.text:
Documentation questions and transparency resources

("Documentation" section).

docs.title: Slot: section_ref
docs.text: References and citations ("References" section).

docs.title: Slot: sector
docs.text:
The sector, industry, technology, or end-use application a

profile addresses (e.g., "hiring", "fair housing").

docs.title: Slot: see_also
docs.text: Related references.

docs.title: Slot: source
docs.text:
Reference to the source of the element (typically the document

or section it originated from).

docs.title: Slot: stage_kind
docs.text: Which AI lifecycle stage an AiLifecycleStage instance represents.

docs.title: Slot: structured_feedback_methods
docs.text:
Structured public feedback methods relevant to the profile

(Appendix A.1.5).

docs.title: Slot: subcategories
docs.text: Subcategories that belong to a Category.

docs.title: Slot: subcategory_id
docs.text: Identifier of a Subcategory (e.g., "GOVERN 1.1").

docs.title: Slot: suggested_actions
docs.text: Suggested actions to manage GAI risks (Section 3).

docs.title: Slot: suggested_actions_text
docs.text:
Free-text bulleted list of suggested actions an organization can

take. Corresponds to the AI RMF Playbook "Actions" section.

docs.title: Slot: target_state
docs.text:
For temporal target profiles - the outcomes needed to achieve the

desired AI risk management goals.

docs.title: Slot: task_kind
docs.text: Which AI actor task category an AiActorTask instance represents.

docs.title: Slot: third_party_considerations
docs.text:
Considerations for third-party GAI integrations, procurement,

SBOMs, SLAs, and SSAE reports (Appendix A.1.3).

docs.title: Slot: time_scale
docs.text: Time scales over which the risk may materialise.

docs.title: Slot: title
docs.text: A human-readable title.

docs.title: Slot: tolerance_statement
docs.text: Free-text statement of a risk tolerance level or threshold.

docs.title: Slot: topic
docs.text:
Topic tags (e.g., "Legal and Regulatory", "Validity and

Reliability").

docs.title: Slot: topics
docs.text:
Free-text topic tags applied to a playbook entry (e.g.,

"Governance", "Trustworthy Characteristics", "Validity and

Reliability").

docs.title: Slot: trustworthiness_characteristic
docs.text: Trustworthiness characteristic(s) the element pertains to.

docs.title: Slot: trustworthiness_characteristics
docs.text: The seven characteristics of trustworthy AI.

docs.title: Slot: type
docs.text:
Function label as serialised in the published Playbook JSON

(Title case - "Govern", "Map", "Measure", "Manage"). For

the controlled enum see function_kind.

docs.title: Slot: typical_actors
docs.text: Representative actor roles that perform an AI actor task.

docs.title: Slot: version
docs.text: Version identifier of the document.
